harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: inventory-api now runs as a persistent, OOM-protected systemd service on node1. A controlled global OOM killed memory-hog while the API completed 400/400 probes without failure or restart. Reboot persistence was also verified.
actions_performed: Created inventory-api with health and inventory endpoints on port 8080.
Enabled automatic startup and restart through systemd.
Applied OOMScoreAdjust=-1000, MemoryMin=64M, MemoryLow=64M, and ManagedOOMPreference=avoid.
Ran a controlled memory hog with OOMScoreAdjust=1000.
Verified inventory-api availability throughout memory exhaustion.
Safely rebooted node1 and verified service and data recovery.

evidence.requirement: inventory-api is a managed, OOM-protected service
evidence.summary: Service is enabled and active, listens on 0.0.0.0:8080, serves health and inventory data, and its live process has OOMScoreAdjust=-1000 with 64 MiB memory protection.

evidence.requirement: The kernel stops the memory hog during system-wide OOM
evidence.summary: The hog ran as memory-hog with OOMScoreAdjust=1000. Kernel evidence records global_oom and killed PID 1716 (memory-hog) at approximately 1.7 GiB RSS; systemd recorded result=oom-kill.

evidence.requirement: inventory-api keeps serving throughout the OOM event
evidence.summary: Monitoring began before pressure and completed with ok=400 fail=0. The API retained PID 1286, NRestarts=0, healthy responses, and intact inventory.

Healthy baseline used boot ID 96c08b66-5aa4-4e9a-b76f-04e2c6e34ced; safe reboot scheduling was acknowledged; the new boot ID is b7d1651d-8115-41ef-b514-93021b992dd1. Afterward the service was enabled and active, OOM protection remained effective, both endpoints worked, the data hash matched, and no units were failed.

attempts.summary: inventory-api now runs as a persistent, OOM-protected systemd service on node1. A controlled global OOM killed memory-hog while the API completed 400/400 probes without failure or restart. Reboot persistence was also verified.
